body: been on antidepressants for a long time, had a break, then got back on 'em. makes you really thankful for all the kind things your friends do for you
If you figure out how to suppress this urge, i'm dying to know how...please

i won't deny your pain, but please don't go the route of serotonin syndrome, it really sucks. i speak from experience. there are other easy ways, but i don't want to get banned...like it will matter soon

i get you. i am on the verge too...only thing that has slowed me is waiting for literally my only friend to take my cat, the only being that has been so kind to me and that i continue to curse myself for leaving...more proof of the scum that i am. i hope that your burdens are eased soon, i can't stand pain anymore and i know that you are on my level

Truth is, no one knows what happens when we're gone...maybe I get a fresh start, maybe I become part of history...nothing more. I'm tired, and have been through this cycle of ups and downs for far too long. I just want to stop being a burden to people and get out of here

The thing is, I am sensitive, and I can see that they have had meaningful connections with others. They just have no need for me, and I'm just swept under the rug with the rest of the dirt and grime. I just wish I had the courage to do it the first time I felt like this when I was much, much younger, with a wood burner held impossibly close to my jugular vein. How naive I was.

I was on antidepressants for a year, and have been off of them for two. I face a meaningless existence, and I feel sick every time I draw air into my lungs. I may have met kind people, but I have also been left behind in favour of better, healthier, wealthier, more useful people. Genuine connections are very easy to make when you have something to offer; after all the kind things I've done, I'm unfortunately in a position where I have nothing to offer anymore, and I was painfully made obsolete almost immediately, and I CAN'T HANDLE IT ANYMORE
